cards.text: Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet in Judah, has just heard the LORD announce disaster coming on Jerusalem. Now he cries out about his own life. "Woe to me, my mother, that you have borne me, a man of strife and conflict in all the land."

cards.question: Jeremiah says everyone curses him over money he lent or borrowed.

cards.text: No loans. No debts. And EVERYBODY's still cursing him. Friend, that's like getting a collections call when you've never even had a credit card.
Then the LORD speaks: "Surely I will deliver you for a good purpose."

cards.question: The LORD says that in the time of trouble and distress, He will intercede with the enemy.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks a question. Can anyone smash iron, iron from the north, or bronze?

cards.question: The LORD asks if anyone can smash iron from the north, or bronze. What answer is that question pointing to?

answers.text: Only a king can smash it
Anyone with fire can smash it

cards.text: Right. NOBODY. That's not a cookie you snap with your thumb. That's the kind you chip a tooth on.
Then the LORD's words turn. He says wealth and treasures will be given up as plunder, without charge.

cards.question: The LORD says the wealth and treasures will be given up as plunder for all your ___.
Next the LORD says His anger will kindle a fire, and "you" will be enslaved to the enemies. Where?

answers.text: In a land you do not know
In the courts of the temple

cards.text: Now Jeremiah turns back to God. "You understand, O LORD; remember me and attend to me."

cards.question: Jeremiah asks the LORD to do something about his persecutors. What is it?
Jeremiah tells the LORD he endures reproach for his own honor.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah talks about the LORD's words. He says they were found.

cards.question: When the LORD's words were found, what does Jeremiah say he did with them?

cards.text: He ATE them. The Millers used to steal cookie dough right off my counter, but I never once saw anybody eat the RECIPE.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the LORD's words became a heavy burden he could hardly carry.

cards.text: Jeremiah says he never sat with the band of revelers, and he never celebrated with them.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the LORD, "Because Your hand was on me, I sat ___."

cards.text: Jeremiah asks why his pain is unending and his wound won't heal. Then he says something about the LORD that's hard to hear.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the LORD has become like what to him?

cards.text: A mirage. Water that isn't there. Friend, that's raw honesty, and he's saying it straight to God.
So the LORD answers him. And His answer starts with an if.

cards.question: The LORD says that if Jeremiah returns, He will restore him, and Jeremiah will stand in His presence.

cards.text: Then comes a second if. This one's about the words coming out of Jeremiah's mouth.

cards.question: What kind of words does the LORD say Jeremiah must speak to be His spokesman?
The LORD tells Jeremiah that the people must turn to him, but he must not turn to them.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Jeremiah what He will make him to this people. A wall.

cards.question: The LORD says, "I will make you a wall to this people, a fortified wall of ___."

cards.text: BRONZE. That's not a wall, friend, that's a STATEMENT. Meanwhile I spent years stuck behind a drawer front made of particle board.

cards.question: The LORD says the people won't even try to fight against Jeremiah.
The people will fight against Jeremiah, but the LORD says they won't overcome him. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD is with him to save him
The people are too afraid of him
The king's guards will protect him

cards.text: And the LORD's not done promising. He says He will deliver Jeremiah from the hand of the wicked.

cards.question: The LORD also says He will redeem Jeremiah from the grasp of whom?

cards.text: Deliver. Redeem. That's the LORD's last word here. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know what it means when God reaches in and gets you out.

findings.problem: The card says Jeremiah 'has just heard the LORD announce disaster coming on Jerusalem.' That fact comes from Jeremiah 15:1-9, outside the passage, but the card gives no reference for it and cites only Jeremiah 15:10.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card adds nothing new from the passage. Card 2 already said 'everyone curses him' and that it wasn't over money he lent or borrowed. This card repeats that and adds a joke, so it is a recap card.
This story card has four sentences: 'No loans.' 'No debts.' 'And EVERYBODY's still cursing him.' 'Friend, that's like...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card only repeats the answer to card 16 ('He ATE them') and adds a joke. It tells no new part of verse 16, such as 'For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.' It is a recap card.
Card 19 already says Jeremiah never sat with the revelers and never celebrated with them. That rules out the wrong answers 'feasting' and 'singing', so only 'alone' is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Important details in the stop's verses are never told: Jeremiah's plea 'In Your patience, do not take me away' (15:15), 'For I bear Your name' (15:16), and 'for You have filled me with indignation' (15:17). These set up his complaint in 15:18.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 1 says Jeremiah is about to say 'something about the LORD that's hard to hear.' Both wrong answers ('A shelter from the storm' and 'A spring that never dries') are comforting, so the setup rules them out. 'A mirage' is also much shorter than the other two answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'A mirage.' 'Water that isn't there.' 'Friend, that's raw honesty...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'Loud instead of quiet' and 'Short instead of long' are close to silly. They also sound unlike the Bible, so the right answer 'Noble instead of worthless' stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card only repeats the answer to card 10 ('BRONZE') and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card.

The comparison doesn't match the action in the verse. The bronze wall is about not being overcome, but the drawer front is what trapped Papa Dorin. The joke also adds a new detail to his world (a particle board drawer front) that isn't about his bakery.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the closing words of the line ('the grasp of the ruthless'), and no story card gives context to reason from. The right answer is also a different kind of thing from the wrong answers: a description of people, while the wrong answers name nations.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
